Definition: an adverb of confirmation; perhaps intensive of G2228; used only (in the New Testament) before G3303; assuredly:--surely.
BiblicalUsage: Surely, assuredly, the little particle of confirmation that stands before the word for indeed in God's oath to Abraham, saying, surely blessing I will bless thee. The Greek text behind our Bibles carries this particle; the text used by modern editors reads the same oath with a different first word.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God's oath to Abraham is sure twice over, because He swore by Himself, and the little word surely is the sound of a promise that cannot fail.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
